privacy.intro: This notice explains how Prodify processes personal data. It is not legal advice.

blocks.heading: 1. Controller
blocks.body: The operator of the Prodify services is responsible for processing (see App Store listing or support email). Which environment you use also depends on the API URL configured in the app.

blocks.heading: 2. Data we process
blocks.body: We process account data (email, username), technical data required to run the app, and content you create such as studio sessions (times, types, optional notes/mood/tags), streak and friendship data, and push tokens if you enable notifications.

blocks.heading: 3. Purposes and legal bases
blocks.body: Processing is necessary to perform the contract (GDPR Art. 6(1)(b)), to protect security and prevent abuse (legitimate interests, Art. 6(1)(f)), and — where you consented — for push messages (Art. 6(1)(a)).

blocks.heading: 4. Retention
blocks.body: We store data while your account exists. After deletion, we remove associated personal data unless a legal retention obligation applies.

blocks.heading: 5. Your rights
blocks.body: You have the right to access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, and objection where processing relies on legitimate interests. You may withdraw consent at any time with future effect. You may lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority.

blocks.heading: 6. Contact
blocks.body: To exercise your rights or ask questions, use the support address shown in the App Store or in the app.

terms.intro: By using Prodify you agree to these terms. Please read them carefully.

blocks.heading: 1. Service
blocks.body: Prodify helps you track and analyse studio sessions, streaks, and social features among friends. Features and availability may evolve.

blocks.heading: 2. Account
blocks.body: You are responsible for keeping your password secure. Content you submit must not infringe third-party rights or violate applicable law.

blocks.heading: 3. Subscriptions
blocks.body: Prodify requires an active subscription. Payment is charged to your Apple ID account at confirmation of purchase. Subscriptions renew automatically unless canceled at least 24 hours before the end of the current billing period. Manage or cancel in Settings > Apple ID > Subscriptions.

blocks.heading: 4. Availability
blocks.body: We strive for high availability but cannot guarantee uninterrupted access — for example during maintenance or force majeure.

blocks.heading: 5. Liability
blocks.body: To the extent permitted by law, we are liable for intent and gross negligence. For slight negligence we are liable only for breaches of essential contractual duties and limited to typical, foreseeable damage.

blocks.heading: 6. Changes
blocks.body: We may update these terms. We will notify you of material changes in the app or otherwise as appropriate. Continued use after notice may constitute acceptance where permitted by law.

beatMaking.description: Drums, bass, chords and samples — the foundation of every beat.

drums.label: Drum Programming
drums.description: Build drum patterns that drive the track — kicks, snares, hats, percussion and fills.
drums.practice: Program three versions of one drum loop: main groove, fill and a stripped-back variation.

groove.label: Groove & Feel
groove.description: Make patterns breathe with swing, velocity and small timing shifts off the grid.
groove.practice: Take a stiff loop and give it feel using only swing and velocity — no new sounds.

bass.label: Bass & 808
bass.description: Write basslines and tune 808s so the low end locks in with the kick.
bass.practice: Tune your 808 to the key of the track and rewrite the bassline so it never fights the kick.

chordsMelody.label: Chords & Melody
chordsMelody.description: Choose a key, build chord progressions and write melodic loops that set the mood.
chordsMelody.practice: Write two different progressions in the same key and keep the one that fits the drums best.

sampling.label: Sampling & Chops
sampling.description: Find samples, chop them into playable pieces and flip them into something new.
sampling.practice: Chop one sample into at least eight slices and play a completely new phrase from them.

soundSelection.label: Sound Selection
soundSelection.description: Pick sounds that fit together before processing anything — the fastest route to a good mix.
soundSelection.practice: Swap every drum sound in a finished beat and compare both versions at matched volume.
soundSelection.covers: Drum kits, presets, sample choice, layering choices

mixing.description: Balancing and shaping every element into one clear, powerful mix.

balance.label: Levels & Gain Staging
balance.description: Set clean gain and balance the faders so every element has its place before processing.
balance.practice: Build a rough mix using only faders and panning, then compare it to your processed mix.
balance.covers: Gain staging, faders, rough mix, bus levels

eq.label: EQ
eq.description: Shape each sound's frequencies — remove what's in the way, then enhance what matters.
eq.practice: Clean up muddiness on three tracks using cuts only, no boosts.

dynamics.label: Compression & Dynamics
dynamics.description: Control peaks, add punch and glue elements together with compressors, gates and sidechain.
dynamics.practice: Compress a drum bus and a lead vocal, level-matching before and after to judge the real difference.

saturation.label: Saturation & Color
saturation.description: Add warmth, grit and harmonics with saturation, tape and distortion so sounds cut through without getting louder.
saturation.practice: Saturate your drum bus and bass in parallel, then level-match to hear what the color really adds.
saturation.covers: Tape, tube, distortion, exciters, parallel drive

space.label: Reverb & Delay
space.description: Create depth and space with reverbs and delays without washing out the mix.
space.practice: Place the whole mix in one shared reverb and one delay, using sends only.

stereo.label: Panning & Stereo
stereo.description: Spread elements across the stereo field and keep the mix solid when played in mono.
stereo.practice: Pan every element on purpose, then check the mix in mono and fix whatever disappears.

automation.label: Automation
automation.description: Move levels and effects over time so the mix follows the song instead of standing still.
automation.practice: Automate the level of your lead element through the whole song, section by section.
automation.covers: Volume rides, FX throws, filter sweeps

translation.label: References & Translation
translation.description: Compare against reference tracks and check different speakers so your mix works everywhere.
translation.practice: Level-match a reference track and compare your mix against it on two different playback systems.
translation.covers: Reference tracks, level matching, speakers, headphones

mastering.description: The final polish that makes a mix release-ready on every platform.

tonalBalance.label: Tonal Balance
tonalBalance.description: Make small EQ moves across the whole mix so it feels balanced from low end to air.
tonalBalance.practice: Match the overall tone of a reference track without any EQ move larger than 2 dB.
tonalBalance.covers: Broad EQ, tilt, low end, air

dynamics.label: Dynamics
dynamics.description: Gently control the mix's dynamics with glue compression, multiband or dynamic EQ.
dynamics.practice: Add glue compression with only 1–2 dB of gain reduction and compare at matched volume.

loudness.label: Limiting & Loudness
loudness.description: Reach a competitive level with a limiter while keeping punch, true peak and LUFS in check.
loudness.practice: Master one track to around −14 LUFS and one louder, then decide which keeps more punch.

stereo.label: Stereo Image
stereo.description: Control the width of the master while keeping the low end centered and mono-safe.
stereo.practice: Keep everything below 120 Hz centered and compare your master's width to a reference.

references.label: References & Metering
references.description: Judge your master with level-matched references and meters, not just by ear.
references.practice: Compare your master to three level-matched references using a spectrum and loudness meter.

delivery.label: Delivery & Sequencing
delivery.description: Finish the release: fades, track order, spacing, metadata and the right export for each platform.
delivery.practice: Prepare final exports with clean fades and correct formats, then do a full quality-control listen.

soundDesign.description: Creating and shaping your own sounds with synths, samples and effects.

synthesis.label: Synthesis Basics
synthesis.description: Build sounds from scratch with oscillators, filters and envelopes.
synthesis.practice: Design a bass, a pad and a pluck from an init patch — no presets.

advancedSynthesis.label: FM & Wavetable
advancedSynthesis.description: Go beyond subtractive with FM, wavetable, granular and additive synthesis.
advancedSynthesis.practice: Create a bell or a growl using only FM or wavetable movement.

modulation.label: Modulation
modulation.description: Bring sounds to life with LFOs, envelopes and macros that move them over time.
modulation.practice: Take a static patch and add three modulations that make it evolve over eight bars.

sampling.label: Sampling & Resampling
sampling.description: Turn recordings and found sounds into instruments, then resample and reshape them.
sampling.practice: Record an everyday sound and turn it into a playable instrument.

effects.label: FX & Processing
effects.description: Transform sounds with distortion, waveshaping and creative effect chains.
effects.practice: Build one effect chain that turns a clean sound into something unrecognizable.
effects.covers: Distortion, waveshaping, effect chains, creative FX

layering.label: Layering
layering.description: Combine several sounds into one bigger sound where every layer has a clear job.
layering.practice: Build a lead from three layers — body, top and texture — and group them into one sound.

recording.description: Capturing clean, inspired performances at the source.

micTechnique.label: Mic Technique
micTechnique.description: Choose and place microphones to capture the sound you want at the source.
micTechnique.practice: Record the same source from three mic positions and compare the takes.

vocals.label: Recording Vocals
vocals.description: Capture clean, confident vocal takes — mic distance, pop control, headphone mix and a good performance.
vocals.practice: Record one verse at three mic distances with a pop filter and keep the take that sounds closest and cleanest.
vocals.covers: Mic distance, pop filter, headphone mix, performance

gainStaging.label: Gain Staging & Signal Flow
gainStaging.description: Set clean input levels and understand how your signal travels from source to DAW.
gainStaging.practice: Record a full take with peaks between −12 and −6 dBFS and no clipping.
gainStaging.covers: Input levels, interface, signal flow, headroom

room.label: Room & Acoustics
room.description: Tame reflections and noise so your recordings sound clean and focused.
room.practice: Record in two different spots of your room and keep the one with fewer reflections.

tracking.label: Tracking & Takes
tracking.description: Run efficient sessions with punch-ins, loop recording and well-organized takes.
tracking.practice: Record one part in several loop takes and mark the best ones while you go.

instruments.label: Recording Instruments
instruments.description: Capture guitars, keys, bass and drums with the right setup for each.
instruments.practice: Record one instrument with two sources (DI and mic, or two mics) and blend them.

songwriting.description: Writing the song itself — melody, chords, lyrics and hooks.

melody.label: Melody & Topline
melody.description: Write memorable melodies with strong motifs, clear shape and natural phrasing.
melody.practice: Write a topline, then develop its main motif into a second, contrasting section.

harmony.label: Harmony
harmony.description: Choose chords and progressions that carry the emotion of the song.
harmony.practice: Reharmonize one finished section using at least one borrowed chord.

lyrics.label: Lyrics
lyrics.description: Write lyrics with a clear idea, vivid images and phrasing that fits the melody.
lyrics.practice: Rewrite one verse with concrete images and make sure every line sings naturally.

songForm.label: Song Form
songForm.description: Write sections — verse, pre-chorus, chorus, bridge — that each have a clear role.
songForm.practice: Write a pre-chorus or bridge for an existing song idea.

hooks.label: Hooks
hooks.description: Create the part people remember — a lyric, melody or rhythm that sticks.
hooks.practice: Write three different hook ideas for one song and keep the strongest.

arrangement.description: Turning ideas into a full track that builds, moves and holds attention.

structure.label: Structure
structure.description: Lay out your track's sections on the timeline and decide how long each one lasts.
structure.practice: Turn an 8-bar loop into a full structure from intro to outro.

transitions.label: Transitions
transitions.description: Connect sections with fills, risers, reverse FX or silence so every change feels earned.
transitions.practice: Give every section change in your track its own distinct transition.
transitions.covers: Fills, risers, reverse FX, drops to silence

energy.label: Energy & Tension
energy.description: Plan how energy rises and falls, with build-ups, drops and breakdowns that pay off.
energy.practice: Sketch an energy curve for your track and adjust the sections until they follow it.

variation.label: Variation & Contrast
variation.description: Keep listeners hooked by adding, removing or changing elements every 8–16 bars.
variation.practice: Make every repeat of your main section differ by at least one element.

instrumentation.label: Instrumentation
instrumentation.description: Decide which elements play where so every section has the right density and focus.
instrumentation.practice: Make one crowded section clearer by removing two elements or adding a single counter-melody.

vocalProduction.description: Taking raw vocals to a finished, polished performance.

comping.label: Comping & Editing
comping.description: Assemble the best phrases from multiple takes and clean up breaths, noises and levels.
comping.practice: Comp a lead vocal from at least three takes with inaudible crossfades.

tuning.label: Tuning & Timing
tuning.description: Correct pitch and timing — transparently or as an audible effect.
tuning.practice: Tune one vocal naturally, then duplicate it and tune the copy as a hard effect.

chain.label: Vocal Chain
chain.description: Shape the vocal with EQ, compression, de-essing and saturation in a deliberate order.
chain.practice: Build a vocal chain from scratch and save it as your own template.

fx.label: Vocal FX
fx.description: Place the vocal in space and add character with reverb, delay throws and creative effects.
fx.practice: Add delay throws on the last word of three different lines.

layering.label: Doubles & Harmonies
layering.description: Stack doubles, harmonies and ad-libs to make vocals wider and fuller.
layering.practice: Add a double and a harmony to the chorus and mix them to sit under the lead.
